absent: Doorbell IRQ registration site, lifetime of the handler binding, and re-enable path.
Virtual PE residency and non-residency sequence that orders against the pending marker.
Definitions of the interrupt target oracle and the pending evaluation used by ordering.
Full ITS device, collection and translation-table management beyond record layouts.
VMID allocation, rollover and per-CPU synchronization beyond sizing and storage.
VGIC global initialization and CPU-interface capability negotiation beyond the initial value.
Hardware semantics of the v5 PPI direct-injection bitmap and delivery guarantees.
Validation and error handling for invalid VCPU, interrupt id or collection references.

findings.text: Provides the PPI queue operation for the v5 path. Its contract requires the interrupt lock already held on entry, releases that lock with flags restored, ensures the target VCPU is marked as having pending interrupt work and is woken, and always reports success.

Provides the PPI direct-injection control for the v5 path. It requires the interrupt lock held, derives the hardware PPI number from the virtual interrupt number, and records the requested direct-injection state in the per-VCPU PPI bitmap.
Clears any custom per-interrupt operations for a given virtual interrupt on a VCPU, leaving no handler installed.
Predicate reporting whether a VM has the GICv5 CPU interface feature enabled, based on the architecture feature register for the GCIE field.
Binds the v5 PPI behaviour table so queueing uses the unlocking queue operation and direct-injection control uses the PPI DVI setter.
Serves as the host interrupt handler for the virtualization doorbell. It guarantees the VPE pending marker ends set, the VCPU is flagged for interrupt work and woken, and handled status is reported.
Serves as the ordering callback for sorting the active and pending interrupt list, imposing a deterministic deliverability and priority order for a given VCPU and control state.
The VPE pending marker update is protected by the per-VPE lock, held across the update so concurrent residency changes cannot interleave.
The unlocking queue operation must be entered with the interrupt lock held and releases it with interrupt state restored. The lock is not held when the VCPU wakeup is issued.
The PPI direct-injection setter requires the interrupt lock held throughout its update of the per-CPU bitmap.
Comparison takes both interrupt locks with a defined nesting order and releases both before returning, so the ordering decision observes a consistent pair.

List order prefers interrupts deliverable to the requesting VCPU over others, then group-enabled over group-disabled under the given controls, then enabled pending non-active over the rest, then lower priority value first, then hardware-backed over purely virtual.
Refire suppression by disabling the doorbell line applies only on non-v4p1 systems and only when the line is not already disabled.
The short PPI capability name is an alias for the corresponding field in the global VGIC state.
The global VGIC state is write-protected after boot and starts with the v3 CPU-interface capability disabled.

VMID sizing derives from the configured bit width. The first version value is one shifted by that width, the user count equals that value, the mask is the complement of the low-bits mask, and the invalid active marker equals the first version.
VMID allocation state uses a monotonically increasing generation counter, a bitmap for in-use values, and per-CPU records of the active value and reserved value.
Sort context pairs a target VCPU reference with a snapshot of the virtual machine control state used for group-enable decisions.

Virtual machine control state holds enable bits for v5 and both interrupt groups, plus acknowledgement, fast-interrupt enable, binary-point controls, end-of-interrupt mode, active and binary points and a priority mask in CPU-interface priority format.
Register access context pairs a VCPU reference with a guest physical address.
ITS device record links siblings and translation entries, and carries the event-ID width, the translation-table address and the device identifier.
ITS collection record links siblings and carries a collection identifier plus a target address.
ITS translation entry links siblings and binds an interrupt record and a collection with an event identifier.
Active and pending list summary counts purely pending entries, active or active-plus-pending entries, and software-generated entries.
Product identity is 0x4B, implementer identity is 0x43B, and the undefined VGIC address marker is negative one.
Shared-interrupt identifier width is ten bits, ITS identifier width is sixteen bits, the largest LPI identifier is two to the sixteen minus one, and priority width is five bits.
Affinity bytes sit at shifts zero, eight, sixteen and twenty-four with eight-bit masks, and level extraction isolates the selected byte then shifts it by the MPIDR level shift.

System-register encoding uses two-bit OP0 at shift fourteen with mask 0xC000, three-bit OP1 at shift eleven with mask 0x3800, four-bit CRN at shift seven with mask 0x0780, four-bit CRM at shift three with mask 0x0078, three-bit OP2 at shift zero with mask 0x0007, with the device mask being the union of all five.
The fixed SRE value enables SRE with DIB and DFB behaviours, the VTR zero-reserved set covers DVIM plus A3V plus ID width, and the VTR one-reserved bit is the no-v4 marker.

Collection entries mark validity at bit sixty-three with redistributor base at shift sixteen and collection id in low sixteen. Translation entries use next at shift forty-eight, physical id spanning bits forty-seven to sixteen at shift sixteen, and collection id in low sixteen. Device entries mark validity at bit sixty-three with next spanning bits sixty-two to forty-nine at shift forty-nine, table address spanning bits forty-eight to five at shift five, and size in low five. Level-one entries mark validity at bit sixty-three with address spanning bits fifty-one to sixteen.

Redistributor descriptor packs index in bits eleven to zero, flags in bits fifteen to twelve at shift twelve, base spanning bits fifty-one to sixteen, and count spanning bits sixty-three to fifty-two at shift fifty-two.
The unmapped-collection sentinel is the all-ones thirty-two-bit value.
Doorbell interrupt request behaviour combines no automatic enabling with unlazy disabling and no balancing.
This translation unit enables trace-point generation, and the VGIC header is protected against multiple inclusion by its include guard.
A v4p1 doorbell may arrive while the virtual PE is being made non-resident, so the pending update must be ordered after that sequence completes.
Sorting may compare an entry with itself on long lists, which must be treated as equal without taking locks twice.
Doorbell handling moves from message receipt to refire suppression, then to pending marking under protection, then to VCPU notification, ending in handled completion.
